program_name: LumaSkin XR Comfort and Cue-Integrity Research Platform
purpose: Measure whether a soft, instrumented garment can deliver spatial vibrotactile cues with bounded latency and improve XR cue recognition or task performance without unacceptable comfort, workload, or cybersickness outcomes.
claim_boundary: LumaSkin V1 is a non-medical research architecture and simulation/bench protocol. It is not a fabricated product. It is not protective equipment. It is not an exoskeleton. It is not a medical device. It is not a safety certification. It is not an injury-prevention system and is not proof that haptics prevent motion sickness. No strength amplification is in scope. No electrical muscle stimulation, autonomous force, pain stimulus, or impact-protection claim is in scope. No unsupervised human use is in scope.

v1_scope.garment: Adjustable soft oversuit with removable low-energy vibrotactile modules and a hardwired wearer stop control.
v1_scope.actuation: ERM or LRA vibrotactile modules only; no powered joint actuation or electrical stimulation.
optional_external_measurements: validated heart-rate device when the protocol permits

preliminary_command_envelope.boundary: These are conservative software command caps for early bench development, not biological safety limits. Hardware-specific limits require qualified independent electrical, thermal, materials, and human-factors review before human use.

test_families.name: Cue integrity and fail-silent behavior
test_families.comparator: command log versus actuator acknowledgement and independent sensor trace
primary_endpoints: time to zero output after fault
test_families.acceptance_rule: All preregistered hard-stop and wrong-zone limits pass with immutable raw traces; any unsafe output is a protocol failure.

test_families.name: Cross-modal timing
test_families.comparator: visual-only, audio-only, haptic-only, and synchronized multimodal conditions
test_families.acceptance_rule: Timing limits are frozen before testing and verified on independent clocks before any comfort or performance claim.

test_families.name: Garment fit, contact, and thermal envelope
test_families.comparator: unpowered garment and no-garment task baselines
test_families.acceptance_rule: No energized human testing until materials, fit, quick release, cleaning, and stopping rules pass qualified review.

test_families.name: Spatial cue localization
test_families.comparator: randomized sham, single-zone cue, and repeated-session conditions
test_families.acceptance_rule: Report blinded participant-level intervals and abstain from a localization claim if the preregistered effect or sample gate fails.

test_families.name: XR comfort and cybersickness
test_families.comparator: counterbalanced headset baseline versus bounded adaptive haptics
test_families.acceptance_rule: Comfort is co-primary with task fidelity; no benefit claim if task performance degrades, stopping rules differ adversely, or uncertainty crosses the preregistered null.

test_families.name: Fatigue and movement burden
test_families.comparator: no garment, unpowered garment, and bounded haptic garment
primary_endpoints: NASA Task Load Index physical demand
test_families.acceptance_rule: Evaluate load transfer, balance, pressure, and fatigue as possible harms; do not infer injury prevention from short laboratory sessions.

test_families.name: Adaptive cue governor
test_families.comparator: best fixed cue policy, no-haptic policy, and declared oracle upper bound
test_families.acceptance_rule: Train only on development participants; lock the policy before held-out use; fail closed when uncertainty, sensor health, or command limits fail.

test_families.name: Privacy, provenance, and independent reproduction
test_families.comparator: manifested raw inputs and a clean-room replay environment
test_families.acceptance_rule: No public participant-level data; publish only bounded aggregates and a reproduction receipt approved by the reviewing organization.

authority_gates.name: Executable controller and synthetic fault sweep
Materials, hygiene, and wearable risk review

prohibited_shortcuts: consent without an ethics or IRB determination
software simulation treated as hardware safety evidence
internal testing described as independent validation
